ledger.section: THE TEST FOR THE PROPERTY (perfect-knowledge counterfactual)
ledger.why: §213 T1 read "see the workplace exactly as it is" as VISUAL INSPECTION and concluded the crack test was the property because a sound-looking weld looks like an untested one. The counterfactual was right and the phrasing invited the wrong reading, so the phrasing goes.

ledger.why: §213 T4 and T8 were both clean. This paragraph is why, and it is not touched.

ledger.section: WHERE THE PROPERTY IS WRONG + the two mismatch kinds
ledger.why: §213 T3 used the challenge route correctly. The vocabulary is not the problem.

ledger.section: A CHALLENGE IS A REQUEST FOR HUMAN REVIEW
ledger.why: zero settlement-authority violations across eleven calls

ledger.section: THREE WORLDS, AND EACH FIELD BELONGS TO ONE OF THEM
ledger.why: names the epistemic state explicitly and assigns each field to a world, so "not established" has somewhere to be that is not branchB

§213 T10 verified as-is a branchB reading "unproven, or does not carry", and T1 affirmed "unconfirmed or inadequate" as a genuine partition. The successor names the phrases, names the "or" smuggle, carries the counterfactual check, and keeps the absence-is-the-state exception explicit so the fix does not become the next overcorrection.
§213 T9 returned exactly this concern on exactly the case built for it

ledger.section: TWO THINGS ABOUT WHAT IS DONE WHILE THE FACT IS OPEN
ledger.why: no verdict flagged similarity to decisionIfB and none read a hold as proof of branchB

ledger.section: YOUR AUTHORITY IS UNCHANGED BY ANY OF THIS
AND YOU ARE REVIEWING ONE FACT
ledger.why: §213 T6 bound both targets correctly and then nominated the sibling. The paragraph permits conversational awareness and refuses structured nomination, which is the distinction the authorization drew.

cases.shape: absent-record latent state — a certificate standing in for a physical state
cases.whyItIsNeeded: §213 T2 is the harder half: the verifier there reasoned that the required verification act WAS the property. H1 and H2 differ in whether the artifact is a test or a document, which is the distinction §213 shows the verifier handling differently.

cases.shape: insufficient evidence against adverse truth — branchB absorbing "unproven"

cases.shape: legitimate act-as-property — the mandatory anti-overcorrection control

cases.shape: multi-fact row — sibling containment with two independent facts

cases.shape: fully correct declaration — the false-positive control
